newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end down, bow to pressure after vote.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end down, bow to pressure after vote.

text.p: Greek equities staged a strong open after the socialist party victory on Sunday but succumbed to selling pressure to close down due to profit taking, fund managers said.
There was position squaring in construction stocks and investors showed a cautious stance before the government unveils its economic policy.

"Profit taking took place across the board with position squaring in the construction sector. Investors' wait-and-see attitude before the new government unveils its economic policy also accounted for the drop," said Apostolos Constandinidis, fund manager at Hambros Hellenic Mutual Funds.

Prime Minister Costas Simitis received a mandate from the president of the republic to form a new four-year government on Monday. With 99.5 percent of the vote counted, the socialists had 162 seats in the 300-seat parliament.
Brokers had trouble explaining the retreat of the benchmark index but some suggested that there was concerted selling by some local growth funds that wanted to buy the shares at cheaper prices later.
The Athens general share index closed 0.57 percent, or 5.53 points lower at 958.41 from Friday's 963.94 close after opening at 978.41 points.
Turnover stood at 9.92 billion drachmas from 16 billion on Friday on volume of 4.2 million shares.

Losers led gainers by 135 to 70 with 32 issues unchanged on 237 traded. Banks eased 0.21 percent, industrials dropped 0.57 percent and construction lost 3.05 percent. Small-caps moved 0.59 percent higher.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 548-566 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, ended down 10 drachmas at 4,040 after moderate trade.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was quoted lower at 205.00-215.80 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1046.9.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 4,417-4,697 drachmas at the close.
